summary: A CCC-built steel fire tower in Trail of Tears State Forest, Illinois, dated 1934-1938 by most accounts; NRHP-listed in 2003, and a 2017 visit found its top unreachable.

facts.design: Steel tower, 80 ft, with a 7-by-7-foot cab (NHLR)

access.note: Clio, citing a park map, says the tower appears to be closed. A July 2017 register visit report says access to the top is not possible.

visit.trail_note: Beside South Forest Road in Trail of Tears State Forest. The 2017 visit report found most wooden steps missing or rotten and no access to the top.

events.note: Wikipedia says circa 1934; Clio says built in 1934 by the CCC. The register gives 1936-1938. Conflict noted.
Register says constructed between 1936 and 1938 by the CCC
Used through the 1960s, per Wikipedia. Year is approximate.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places February 5, 2003 (ref. 02001759)
Visit report of July 5, 2017: top not accessible, most wooden steps missing or rotten, paint failing

corrections.why: The register describes an 80-foot steel tower, which is 24.4 m. The 100-foot figure (30.5 m) appears only in Clio. The register is preferred, but the editor should confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1936-1938. Wikipedia says circa 1934, Wikidata gives a 1934-1935 range, and Clio says 1934. The story gives both and flags the disagreement.
The register gives 80 ft (24.4 m). Clio gives 100 ft (30.5 m). Wikipedia gives no height. The register figure is used in the facts.
The register names the Illinois Department of Conservation. Wikidata names the Illinois Department of Natural Resources. The sources name different state agencies, so the story reports both.
Clio calls it Trail of Tears State Park. The register and Wikipedia say Trail of Tears State Forest. The story uses State Forest.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination (Schroeder, 2002) was not readable; the catalog.archives.gov PDF returned no extractable text, so NRHP details come from Wikipedia. Build year (1934 vs 1936-1938) and height (80 vs 100 ft) conflict across sources. The closed status comes from Clio's reading of a park map and should be checked with the park office. The 2017 visit report is the most recent condition evidence found.
